*   If you haven't been to Gunan Street, you haven't been to Yixing.
How can you not visit Gunan Street when you come to Yixing?
Although the scenic spot is not big, many Yixing clay teapot craftsmen gather here, and many cultural masters have visited.
Shushan Gunan Street is located in Dingshu Town, Yixing City, with the Li River to the south and Shushan Mountain to the north.
The street is 1,000 meters long and only three or four meters wide.
It has been a distribution center for the production, trade, and distribution of Yixing clay teapots since the Ming and Qing Dynasties.
Gunan Street was formed in the Ming Dynasty.

During the Ming and Qing Dynasties, it was the main distribution center for Yixing ceramics, the birthplace of Yixing clay teapots, and the production and sales center of Yixing clay teapots from the mid-Ming Dynasty to the 1960s.
Later, with the development of land transportation, the production center of Yixing clay teapots moved to Dingshan, and Shushan became quiet.
In 1996, it was included in the municipal-level cultural relics protection unit.
The buildings are all two-story brick and wood structures, mostly 1-2 story commercial storefronts.
The style and form are basically well preserved, with the unique characteristics of being close to the mountains and rivers and integrating life and production.

More than half of the residents here used to be engaged in the production and operation of Yixing clay teapots, and many Yixing clay teapot masters, such as Ren Ganting and Gu Jingzhou, have emerged from here.
It is a veritable cradle for the growth of Yixing clay teapot art masters.
There are also many former employees of the Second Pottery Factory who have been making Yixing clay teapots all their lives and have their own studios here.
If you meet a teapot that catches your eye, you can buy it.
The street is not big, and you can walk through it in an hour.
However, if you want to take a closer look at the Yixing clay teapots and talk to the craftsmen, it may take some time.

*   Yixing｜Great for Shopping, Come Quickly When it comes to Yixing, many people immediately think of Yixing clay teapots.
If you want to learn about Yixing clay teapots and related culture, or even experience making one yourself, you must visit Dingshu Town in Yixing.
There are two main places to go here: one is Shushan Ancient South Street; the other is the Second Pottery Factory, which are only about 200 meters apart. ⚠️ Why say don’t come lightly?

Because there are so many small items, it’s easy to get overwhelmed and hard to keep moving, plus you might impulsively spend money and place orders. 📌 Shushan Ancient South Street This area was the core of Yixing clay pottery production and trade during the Ming and Qing dynasties.
It is named after the Shushan Mountain behind it, which made it convenient to source clay; in front is the Li River, which facilitated transportation.
The existing old street stretches for a kilometer and includes the former residences of masters like Gu Jingzhou and 34 historical buildings such as the Yixing Clay Potters’ Guild.

Walking here, you can feel the comfortable and leisurely lifestyle of Jiangnan. 📌 Second Pottery Factory Originally established in the 1980s as the Second Yixing Clay Factory, it has now been transformed into a comprehensive cultural and commercial street integrating cultural creativity, art exhibitions, and lifestyle experiences.

The UCCA Tao Art Museum, designed by Kengo Kuma, is rich in Yixing clay elements and full of detailed design, making it a popular spot for social media check-ins. 🛍️ Shopping Tips You can find some unique shops in both places.
Nowadays, these are run by various “curators” of Yixing clay, bringing creative Yixing clay works where you can find great items.
Shushan Ancient South Street’s shops are generally smaller and prices are relatively lower, making it easier to learn about Yixing clay knowledge and culture.
The Second Pottery Factory is a newly developed area with better planning, larger shops, and a wider variety of products.
It also has more restaurants and coffee shops. ⚠️ So it’s recommended to visit Shushan Ancient South Street first.
If you see something you like, you can buy it first, but don’t be too impulsive.
